title: The fair-test repair lab
subtitle: Spring 2 • Week 5 • One change, useful evidence
objective: Plan and use a fair test of how card height affects shadow height.

sow.exactOutcome: Plan and carry out a fair test about shadows or reflection.
sow.alignment: Direct match to the named outcome. The lesson is a 40-minute exemplar, with optional greater depth; no accreditation completion is claimed.

priorLearning: Everyday objects can be described by what we observe.
Use a labelled diagram or evidence card to explain a choice.
success: Identify the intended change, measurement and controls.
Repair a plan that changes two factors.
Use repeated readings to make a supported conclusion.

vocabulary.meaning: A comparison changing one chosen factor while keeping relevant others the same.
Do a measurement again under the same conditions.
Information used to support an explanation or decision.

equipment: Low-power small LED source; fixed white screen; opaque cards 2, 4 and 6 cm high of same material and width; ruler; stands; printed plans and readings.
preparation: Fix source-screen distance at 60 cm and card position at 30 cm from source. Keep cards upright, centred and parallel to screen.
Pre-cut three cards of the same width and material. Card height is the intended changed factor.
Pre-check that the shadow fits the screen and ruler. Provide constructed readings if the practical cannot run.
safety: Use a cool low-power LED below face height, never a laser, hot lamp or Sun.
Secure stands and card holders, keep walkways lit and clear. Adult checks the practical plan before use.
Use pre-cut cards with safe edges. Do not put a ruler or head in the beam near the source.
practicalAlternative: Analyse the flawed/repaired plans and supplied constructed repeats. Pupils can complete a fair-test plan and conclusion without taking measurements.

misconceptions.claim: Any two different results show what caused the change.
misconceptions.correction: If several factors change, their effects cannot be separated by that comparison.
misconceptions.check: Ask what changed in the flawed plan.

misconceptions.claim: A different repeat should be deleted.
misconceptions.correction: Keep the reading, check the method and repeat if useful; do not remove it just to fit a pattern.
misconceptions.check: Ask what to do with the 9 cm reading.

misconceptions.claim: Fair means everybody must get exactly the same number.
misconceptions.correction: Fair concerns the comparison; measurements can vary even with a careful method.
misconceptions.check: Ask why repeated measurements are useful.

access.supported: Choose one route: short choices, word bank and pointing or adult-scribed explanation; keep the same science goal.
access.standard: Use the evidence provided to record a decision and explain the science in short sentences.
access.stretch: Apply the same core idea to a changed setup, identify a limitation and justify a better decision.
access.regulation: Preview the sequence and equipment. Offer seated observation, a quiet paper route, partner rehearsal and a pass. Never require public performance or a darkened room.

sources.title: Department for Education: science programmes of study
sources.note: Checked 8 September 2026. Year 3 light outcomes anchor the BUILD content; ray explanations are carefully modelled as an accessible extension.

slides.title: Can this test answer its question?
body: Question: do taller cards make taller shadows?
A team changed height and distance.
slides.notes: Invite pupils to act as method reviewers. The goal is a justified repair, not spotting a classmate’s mistakes. Everyone uses the same supplied fictional team.

slides.title: Recall our shadow studio
body: 2. Can moving a card change shadow size?
3. What unit measures our shadow height?
slides.notes: Answers opaque card; yes with setup specified; centimetres. Recall that position matters before introducing the flawed plan.

slides.title: I spot two changed factors
slides.notes: Think aloud: “The question is about card height. But I count two changes: height and distance. Distance can affect shadows, so I cannot say height alone caused any difference.”

visual.title: Two changes muddle the answer
visual.description: Two tests use cards with different heights. One card is 30 cm and the other 20 cm from the source, so both height and distance change.

elements.text: Same screen position: 60 cm from the source.

slides.title: I repair the comparison
slides.notes: Think aloud: “I keep the same source and screen 60 cm apart. Each card stays 30 cm from the source. I also keep material, width and orientation the same. Now height is the intended difference.”

visual.title: One change at a time
visual.description: Two tests use cards with different heights. Both cards are placed 30 cm from the source, with a fixed screen 60 cm from the source.

elements.text: Same screen position: 60 cm from the source.

slides.title: I measure and repeat consistently
body: Measure bottom to top in centimetres.
Use the same edge rule each time.
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Model zero at bottom and 8 cm at top. For repeats, check the same setup and read again; repositioning the card carefully between trials can check placement consistency. Do not silently switch to width or another ruler origin.

visual.title: Measure one height in centimetres
visual.description: Front-view screen with a rectangular shadow beside a ruler. The shadow runs from zero to eight centimetres; use the same top-to-bottom measure each time.

elements.text: Measure from the bottom edge to the top edge.

slides.title: Make a test contract
slides.notes: Give pairs three headings: change / measure / keep same. Use plan cards A and B. Height is changed; shadow height measured; source-card and source-screen distances controlled, plus card material/width/orientation and source.
slides.prompt: W1. Which choices answer our height question?
slides.reveal: Change card height; measure shadow height; keep card position the same.

slides.title: What should we do with 9?
slides.notes: Use the shared reading table. 4 cm card has 8, 8 and 9 cm shadows. Do not erase 9 to make a perfect double pattern. Suggest checking ruler zero, edges, alignment and card position, then repeat. All three card-height groups still support taller card → taller shadow in this setup.

table.caption: Constructed teaching readings, not class observations

slides.prompt: W2. Can we keep a useful conclusion and keep the 9?
slides.reveal: Yes. Taller cards gave taller shadows here. Keep 9, check the setup and repeat if needed.

slides.title: Which plan is fair for this question?
body: Question: how does card height affect shadow height?
slides.notes: If A chosen, point back to distance effects. If C, explain that keeping the card height unchanged does not test its effect.

options.text: Change card height and source distance together.
options.feedback: Two changes mean we cannot separate their effects.

options.text: Change card height; keep the source, screen and card position fixed.
options.feedback: This isolates the intended change, with other relevant properties also controlled.

options.text: Keep card height the same and only change its colour.
options.feedback: That tests a different question, not the effect of height.

slides.title: Choose your investigation route
body: Review the strength of a claim.
slides.notes: Give one route only, selected with the pupil. The shared evidence page supports every route. Practical option after adult plan check: test each card at the fixed holder position and take three readings, using the same shadow-height rule. Keep actual values separate from the constructed table. Paper reviewers use the plans and readings to complete the full objective.

slides.title: Use the evidence
body: Read or point to one clue.
slides.notes: Shares the 12-minute independent stage. Practical option after adult plan check: test each card at the fixed holder position and take three readings, using the same shadow-height rule. Keep actual values separate from the constructed table. Paper reviewers use the plans and readings to complete the full objective.

slides.title: Make your own science record
body: Use a diagram, words or speech.
Check one answer with the evidence.
slides.notes: Allow ten minutes of independent response after the two-minute setup. Practical option after adult plan check: test each card at the fixed holder position and take three readings, using the same shadow-height rule. Keep actual values separate from the constructed table. Paper reviewers use the plans and readings to complete the full objective.

slides.title: Check and improve
body: Does my answer match the evidence?
slides.notes: Shares the independent stage. Ask the pupil to point to the clue supporting their answer; accept a spoken correction or changed choice.

slides.title: Lundy loop: improve our account
body: Choose how to share one idea.
Use evidence to improve our account.
slides.notes: Give a private or paired option. Adopt one scientifically sound pupil revision in the class explanation and name the change. No public ranking.
slides.reveal: A clear question, one intended change, controlled comparisons and honest repeated readings.

slides.title: Three quick checks
body: E1. What factor did this test change?
E2. Name one thing kept the same.
E3. Should we delete a different reading just to fit the pattern?
slides.notes: Collect brief individual answers. Secure core requires the main idea and a relevant reason. Revisit the relevant worked diagram next lesson if the explanation reverses cause and effect.
slides.reveal: See the teacher answer guide for the three checks.

pupilPages.title: Evidence: plans and repeated readings
pupilPages.intro: Constructed teaching cases and readings. Source and screen are 60 cm apart.

cards.title: A • Flawed comparison
cards.text: 2 cm card: 30 cm from source. 4 cm card: 20 cm from source.

cards.title: B • Repaired comparison
cards.text: Each card: 30 cm from source. Change height only; keep material, width and orientation the same.

blocks.prompt: W1. Name the change, measurement and one control.
W2. What should the team do with the 9 cm reading?

pupilPages.title: Route 1 • Build a fair-test plan
pupilPages.intro: Word bank: card height / shadow height / same / repeat.

blocks.prompt: S1. What are we deliberately changing?
S2. What are we measuring?
S3. Keep each card __ cm from the source.
S4. Do taller cards give taller or shorter shadows in the table?
S5. What should we do if a reading differs?

pupilPages.title: Route 2 • Record a method and conclusion
pupilPages.intro: Use the repaired plan and readings. Optional practical: use a separate record clearly labelled “our measurements”.

blocks.prompt: T1. Write the investigation question.
T3. Write a short method including a repeat.
T4. Write a conclusion using two values from the table.
T5. Explain what to do with the 9 cm reading.

pupilPages.title: Route 3 • Review the quality of evidence
pupilPages.intro: A team claims: “Our test proves every shadow is exactly twice the card height.”

blocks.prompt: X1. Use the readings to identify a problem with “exactly”.
X2. Explain why the claim cannot cover every possible setup.
X3. Write a more careful conclusion for this setup.
X4. Suggest one method check and one extra reading that would improve confidence.

pupilPages.title: Exit and reflection
pupilPages.intro: Point, draw, write or tell an adult.

blocks.prompt: E1. What factor did this test change?
E2. Name one thing kept the same.
E3. Should we delete a different reading just to fit the pattern?
R1. Which idea did you improve after hearing evidence?
R2. What would you investigate or ask next?

answers.label: Retrieval 1–3
answers.answer: 1 opaque card. 2 yes, card position can affect size. 3 centimetres (cm).

answers.label: We do W1–W2
answers.answer: W1 change card height, measure shadow height, control card position (30 cm) and source-screen distance (60 cm), with other relevant properties fixed. W2 retain 9, check method and repeat if useful; overall taller-card pattern remains supported.

answers.label: Hinge
answers.answer: Second option correct. Also keep material, width, orientation and source the same. First option changes two factors; third tests colour instead of height.

answers.label: S1–S5
answers.answer: S1 card height. S2 shadow height. S3 30 cm. S4 taller. S5 keep it, check the setup and repeat rather than erasing it.

answers.label: T1–T5
answers.answer: T1 how does card height affect shadow height? T2 height; shadow height; any two relevant controls. T3 fix source-screen at 60 cm and card at 30 cm, use same material/width/orientation, change height, measure same top-to-bottom dimension, repeat three times and record all readings. T4 e.g. 2 cm card gave 4 cm shadows, 6 cm card gave 12 cm shadows; taller cards made taller shadows here. T5 retain it, check ruler zero/edges/position and repeat if needed.

answers.label: X1–X4
answers.answer: X1 the 4 cm card includes a 9 cm reading, not exactly double. X2 shadow size also depends on source/card/screen geometry and source size. X3 in this setup, taller cards gave taller shadows, around twice card height. X4 check card position or ruler alignment/edge convention; take another reading for the 4 cm card after the check, retaining the original.

answers.label: Exit E1–E3
answers.answer: E1 card height. E2 e.g. card-source distance, source-screen distance, card material/width/orientation or source. E3 no; keep honest readings and investigate differences.

answers.label: Optional practical
answers.answer: Accept actual observations, including imperfect proportionality. Do not replace measurements with constructed sample values. Assess the fair comparison and evidence-based conclusion.

answers.label: R1–R2
answers.answer: Responses vary. Credit a science-related revision or relevant next question. A pass or private response is acceptable; preferences have no fixed right answer.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2; retrieval 3; I do 7; We do 8; hinge 3; You do 12; review 3; exit 2. Zero-minute slides share the stage time.
BUILD follows the user’s Year 3 science anchor with age-respectful materials for secondary pupils. Routes are adjustable access choices, not fixed groups or diagnoses.
Every core task can run from the printed evidence. Do not present constructed teaching evidence as observations pupils made. A pupil’s spoken reasoning carries the same scientific value as writing.
Do not require averages for the BUILD core. Pupils can compare repeated values, notice a range of 8–9 cm and write “around” or “about”.

The ideal point-source geometry with source-screen distance twice source-card distance predicts doubled shadow height. The constructed 9 cm reading deliberately models measurement variation; it is not a reason to manufacture perfect data.

HTML We do: pupils choose a prediction, test it against the user-controlled SVG model or supplied evidence, then explain or revise. The shared paper cases and W1/W2 prompts provide the equivalent classroom discussion without a device. Any animation is a teaching model, not filmed experimental evidence.

interactive.intro: Review the fictional plan, predict the useful repair, then inspect the evidence. Keep honest readings.
